summary: Amazon Advertising applied paper on CRAFT, a two-stage post-training recipe for an analytics coding agent: schema-stripped supervised fine-tuning on 15.1K filtered trajectories (from 100K+ generations; execution, data-integrity and LLM-judge gates) on an unnamed 120B MoE base, then GRPO with execution-shaped rewards. Against a schema-stuffed baseline that injects 50K+ tokens of DDL/API docs, it reports +9.6 pp composite Agent Score and ~9x fewer input tokens, with all results given only as relative deltas because absolute scores are confidential.

claims.claim: CRAFT improves composite Agent Score by +9.6 pp, consistency +4.1 pp, multi-turn coherence +4.2 pp over the schema-stuffed baseline
claims.evidence: Table 4 (Stage II, ± values over three seeded runs). Only deltas are reported; absolute scores, number of evaluation tasks, baseline model identity, and judge validation are not disclosed. Agent Score weights are not given.

claims.claim: ~9x input-token reduction and schema-discovery loops reduced to 0.20x
claims.evidence: Table 5: input tokens 0.11x for both stages; loops 0.62x (SFT) and 0.20x (SFT+RL). Token reduction follows by construction from removing the 50K+ schema context.

claims.claim: RL, not SFT alone, aligns tool-use/interaction policy
claims.evidence: Table 4 ablation: SFT alone +2.6 Agent Score and −1.4 consistency; SFT+RL +9.6 / +4.1. Internal ablation, three seeds.
Table 8: IFEval +0.6, GSM8K +0.9, GPQA −0.3 pp vs pre-adaptation base; 13-gram GSM8K contamination audit (App. E).

patterns.note: SFT + execution-shaped GRPO internalizes a stable proprietary schema; internal-only evidence.
Execution outcomes gate trajectory acceptance and anchor RL rewards (§3.2, App. C).
LLM-judge ensemble used as filter gate and reward term for plan-code consistency; acknowledged reward-hacking risk, no validation reported (§9, App. C).
Argues against prompt-time schema stuffing/retrieval for stable schemas; limitations concede retrieval is still needed for schema-novel entities.
Reports input-token ratios as a first-class metric.

methodology.sample: 25 schema-linked entities, 30 agentic workflows; number of held-out evaluation tasks not reported
methodology.baselines: Schema-stuffed baseline with exhaustive DDL/API context; baseline model not named (App. A 'strongest schema-stuffed baseline')
methodology.models: Unnamed 120B MoE base; 'larger reference' model in Table 8 unnamed
methodology.variance: Means ± spread over three seeded runs
methodology.contamination_controls: 13-gram GSM8K overlap audit; none needed for proprietary tasks
methodology.languages: Generated analytics code over proprietary APIs; language not specified in sections reviewed

standards.artifacts: None released; schemas, APIs, rubrics, data and absolute scores confidential

biases.detail: Only relative deltas; no data, model, prompts or rubrics.
Authors define Agent Score, rubrics and judges for their own system on their own environment.
Judge signals in filtering, reward and evaluation (plan-code consistency, business alignment) without reported human agreement.
Only baseline is schema stuffing; no retrieval-based or tool-based schema discovery baseline, which is the obvious competing approach.

coi.affiliations: Amazon Advertising Foundations and Amazon Web Services Agentic AI (all listed authors)
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Amazon's own pre-deployment advertising analytics agent over Amazon Ads beta APIs
coi.funding: Amazon (implied by affiliation); no acknowledgments section
coi.detail: Vendor evaluating its own planned product on confidential data with self-defined metrics; no independent replication is possible.

verdict_reason: Interesting design lesson (internalize stable schemas instead of stuffing prompts) with a seeded ablation, but evidence is relative-only, closed, judge-scored, and compared only against a weak schema-stuffing baseline by the vendor itself.
applicability: Weak transfer. A Java team using third-party agent hosts will not post-train a 120B model, and its healthcare-education content schemas evolve across ≥4 repos — exactly the 'schema-novel' case the limitations say CRAFT does not cover. The practical takeaway is the opposite lever: don't stuff full schemas into prompts; expose schema/contract lookup as deterministic tools or on-demand skills, and gate agent output with execution and data-integrity checks before any LLM judge (the Tri-Gate ordering).
